A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPAR study. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and matchable, including material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original SPAR training and evaluation results, including benchmark scores, synthetic experiments, ablations and inference-scaling analyses in Section 3 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 3 and Appendix E, including actor, judgment and refinement evaluations.

M1.justification: The actor/refiner framework, initialization, majority voting, BFS/DFS refinement, DPO actor training and RFT refiner training remain unchanged in Section 2 and Algorithms 1-2.

E1.justification: Both use the same constructed instruction dataset and evaluate on IFEval, FollowBench, LLMBar, GSM8k, TriviaQA, MMLU and HumanEval. The character-sequence and story-generation synthetic tasks are also retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain AutoIF, SELF, Humpback, Self-Rewarding and Meta-Rewarding, alongside unchanged judgment and decoding comparator sets. Although v2's Appendix D says 'four' approaches, it still lists the same five; no comparator was removed.

E3.justification: Sections 3.1-3.2 and Appendix C retain the same model configurations, three iterations with 10k prompts each, training budgets, evaluation metrics, pointwise LLMBar adaptation and 200-example refinement test.

E4.justification: The synthetic interference experiments (Figure 4), component ablations (Tables 4-5), voting and decoding comparisons (Tables 9-10), and inference-scaling analyses (Figures 5 and 10) are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The unchanged majority-voting counts describe decoding rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1-10 and the plotted results retain the same entries, values and trends. For example, Table 1 reports an IFEval average of 81.8 for SPAR-8B-DPO-iter3 in both versions; Table 10 retains BFS scores of 79.0 and 90.5 under the two judges.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and SFT/DPO objectives in Equations (1)-(2) are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theoretical guarantees, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows 'promising scalability and transferability' to 'promising scalability.' The central claims about refinement pairs, iterative self-improvement, surpassing GPT-4-Turbo on IFEval and maintaining general capabilities remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations concerning interfering response variations, adversarial robustness and inference scaling. Section 3.4's qualification about self-evaluation bias is unchanged, and no substantive limitation or mechanism explanation is added.

D1.justification: Appendices A-C preserve the same prompt templates, algorithm listings, hyperparameters, sample counts and eight 80GB A100 GPU setup. The stated code/data availability and access links also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Section 4 retain the same cited works and positioning within instruction-following and autonomous alignment research. Moving the baseline descriptions to Appendix D does not change their substance.

P1.justification: v2 adds conference-publication headers and an acknowledgements section, moves baseline descriptions from Section 3.1 to Appendix D, and relabels the experimental-results appendix from D to E. Other wording and paragraph changes are limited.

P2.justification: Existing figures and tables undergo size, spacing and placement adjustments. Figure 5 moves from page 10 to page 9 and its caption is shortened; appendix displays are redistributed. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The revision preserves the method, experimental evidence and reproducibility information. Its narrower abstract wording and presentation edits are limited, while the relocated baseline list introduces a small 'four' versus five inconsistency. These changes do not materially strengthen or weaken the paper overall.
